Referred to Committees on Jurisprudence, and on Policy and General Purposes.

The Committee. on Policy and General Purposes:
This resolution proposes that each and every Committee of this
Grand Lodge to which any proposed resolution is referred for study and
recommendation be under the specific duty, in every instance, " to state
the specific section or se<:tions of the C.M.C. which are in contradiction
to the proposed resolution, and which Ancient Landmark or Landmarks
and which Ancient Charge or Charges the proposed resolution would
violate."
While the stated purpose of the proposal is to avoid confusing many
of the new members of the Grand Lodge, and while confusion is certainly to be avoided wherever possible, it is doubted that the resolution
is needed in most cases or would be effective in others.
A large proportion of the reports made to this Grand Lodge do not
revolve about suggested violations of our Constitution, Code, Landmarks or Charges. Proposals referred to and reported upon by the
Finance Committee may not violate any Constitution, Code, Landmark
or Charge yet may endanger the financial integrity of our institution.
Proposals are frequently received-some having been reported on already- where no violation is involved but cumbersome and unnecesary
duplications of existing provisions are submitted. Other proposals may
violate nothing , yet create such ambiguities when read with other existing legislation as to require extensive redrafting by the Jurisprudence
Committee. And other proposals are made-again illustrated in reports
already made-where Policy considerations point strongly against resolutions which, if enacted, would not violate our law.
Hence there is a great body of Committee consideration and reporting which is completely outside of the area contemplated by Resolution
No.32.
In those instances where there is what the resolution calls "contradiction to the proposed resolution," your Committee on Policy and Genera l
Purposes seriously doubts whether the confusion, if any. of new members

21S8

PIWCEED1N0S Ol' THI::

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

to Grand Lodge would be lessened if every Committee Report presented
its version of an exhaustive review of all language in our Constiution.
Code and decisions thereunder, as well as pertinent extracts from all
former proceedings-not to mention Landmarks and Ancient Chargesbefore proceeding to the salient points at issue. In reality. Committee reports are sincere attempts to state issues fairly and clearly. citing our
law when and to the extent it is necessarily involved. They attempt to
simplify both the proposals being made and the committees ' recommendations in respect to them-thus opening the issues for full debate by those
who wish to be heard in respect to them. and aiding the members of
Grand Lodge in reaching their own conclusions at the time of voting.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes moves the adoption
of Resolution No. 32 and recommends a "no" vote thereon.

BUDGET COMMENTS

The. Committee on Jurisprudence:
The proposed resolution requests that a function of Grand Lodge
committees shall be to cite any and all California Masonic Code sections
and any and all Ancient Landmark or Landmarks and any and all Ancient Charge or Charges which are in contradiction to proposed resolutions.
Your Committee on Jurisprudence believes that legislation regarding
the purpose of the resolution is unnecessary. Under procedure presently
in effect. Section 191 of the California Masonic Code, all matters, including resolutions , are referred to the appropriate Grand Lodge committees for action and recommendations. Each such committee is charged
to consider any part of our Code affected by the resolution.
Your Committee on Jurisprudence has the specific job of preparing
proper legislation which includes amendments, deletions and substitutions of the applicable Code sections.
Thus no new legislation appears necessary.
W e recommend a "no" vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
In accordance with requirements set out in Section 194, "Audit of
Accounts," California Masonic Code, records and financial statements
of the Grand Lodge of California, the Masonic Homes of California and
the California Masonic Memorial Temple have been examined by certified public accountants for the Grand Lodge year ended June 30, 1968.
Copies of the audit reports have been referred to the members of the
Finance Committee and it is our opinion that the reports correctly state
the financial operations of Grand Lodge nnd its agencies for the flscnl
year July I , 1967 to June 30. 1968.

289

If you will refer to Exhibit B of the audit report for Grand Lodge,
you will note a net revenue of $132,808 which is considerably higher
than has been reported in recent years. Deducting a gain of $19,812
derived from sale of securities, a non-budget operation, we have a net
gain of $112,996 from budget operations.
To begin with, we provided for a cash surplus in the 1967-1968
budget, on and above all revenue and expense operations of $23, 180.
This cash surplus was realized. Our estimates of revenues proved to be
low in tha t an additional gain of $35,093 was realized. Most of this ,
$33.220 came from revenue produced by the per capita of $3.57 established for the Grand Lodge year 1966-1967 and actually received on or
after July 1, 1967. Income from securities held for the benefit of Grand
Lodge was greater than anticipated and produced an additional $7.088
in revenue. A refund of $2.325 was received from Past Grand Master
Dayton representing the unexpended portion of his Grand Master's
travel allowance. Miscellaneous revenues of $1. 773 accounted for the
remainder of revenue gains. Offsetting these gains in part. was a total
of $9.3 13 representing reductions in anticipated revenue from sale of
supplies and publication of the California Freemason.
With respect to budgeted expenses, a substantial saving of $54,723
was realized-attributable to expenditures in several instances being less
than estimated for budget purposes. Principal savings were effected in
the following accounts: Total salaries paid were $10,049 less than
budgeted. With the labor market in a constant state of change, we have
consistently provided for possible emergencies but good management
in the Grand Secretary's office has enabled Grand Lodge to maintain a
good working force at costs less than provided for. With the closing of
the clubhouses on the campuses of the University of California at
Berkeley and Los Angeles. fifty ( 50) per cent of the appropriations for
their operation unused, resulting in a saving of $21.500 in budgeted
expenses. There were a number of accounts in which actual expenditures
were less than budgeted and savings adding up to $23,174 make up the
total savings in budgeted expenses of $54,723.
We call your attention to the fact that there were several instances
where special committees incurred expenses which were not provided for
in the budget and there were also other instances where expenditures
exceeded budgeted amounts. To cover these exceptions, the Grand
Master has approved supplemental appropriations totaling $5,525. said
appropriations being included in our financial statements and in the foregoing section of this report relating to expenses of Grand Lodge.
In accordance with our law, we present the supplemental appropriations and recommend your approval of the action of the Grand Master :

We summarize this section of the report with the comment that the
gain, or net revenue, for the year of $132,808 represents a per capita of
$.56 based on a 1966-1967 taxable membership of 238,302. By comparison, the per capita for 1967-1968 was based on a membership of 236,142.
Our membership this year, for purpose of the per capita to be established
for 1968-1969, will be nearer 235,000. As has been indicated, we prepare
the annual budget hoping to achieve a gain, or net revenue, of approximately $.I 0 per capita. This year we realized, in addition, on a per
capita basis, $.15 on revenue items. $.23 on expense items and $.08 on
capital items, the sale of securities. When gains are achieved they
become a part of the reserves of Grand Lodge-separate from the Endowment Fund or reserves of the Masonic Homes and the Memorial
Temple. It is necessary, of course, that Grand Lodge possess sufficient
reserves to meet contingencies which could confront it. As the Investment
Committee, under the able leadership of the Grand Treasurer, pursues
the "prudent man rule" in the investment of all funds of the Grand
Lodge. so does the Finance Committee recommend a prudent policy in
the expenditure of Grand Lodge funds.
CALIFORNIA FREEMASON

In asking for a per capita tax of $.35 last year for the editing, printing
and distribution of the California Fceemason to the members of our
Jurisdiction , we anticipated a net revenue of $4 ,000 which was not realized, the net being only $22. In the face of rising costs in the printing
and publishing indus tries, we are again accepting the recommendation of
a per capita tax of $.35. You can help Grand Lodge meet its goal if all
Lodges, through their secretaries, maintain a constant check on changes
of addresses of their members and notify Grand Lodge promptly of such
changes. Excess postage for the handling and remailing of copies of the
magazine returned for incorrect addresses runs into a large sum of money
each year and the Grand Secretary solicits your help so that the present
per capita can be maintained.

MASONIC HOMES

You have received _the reports of the Board of Trustees and the
Superintendents of the Masonic Homes. They are reports of accomplishments. One of the highlights of Grand Lodge Week has always
been the annual visit to the Masonic Home at Decato. The expense of
bus transportation to the Home, the lunches furnished and the rest of the
year round operations of the Endowment Board, as a matter of policy,
has been borne by the Trustees of the Masonic Homes through reimbursement to Grand Lodge.
It can be argued that items of expense of the Endowment Board
should be met by the Masonic Homes of California inasmuch as the
activities are productive of contributions to the Endowment Fund without which we would have difficulty in maintaining the Homes. However,
at the request of the Board of Trustees. and in view of its recommendation that the per capita for support of the Homes be reduced from $1.50
to $1.l 5. the Finance Committee is recommending that a change in procedure be made.
We point out that there will be income by way of the $1.50 per
capita tax levied for the Homes last year and available as of July 1, 1968
for expenses in the budget now being presented to you. Consequently,
the expenses in connection with the visit to the Home at Decato and

by the Masonic Homes and these expenses for succeeding years should
be borne by Grand Lodge after the reduced per capita tax is in effect.

under discussion have been averaging about $.10 per capita and that the
proposed reduction in the per capita for the Masonic Homes will be $.35
-a reduction of approximately $.25 in the total per capita to be asked

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

AFTERNOON SESSION-Friday, October 18, 1968
At 2 :00 p.m. Grand Lodge was called on, the Grand Master presid·
ing. This session was raised by Worshipful George W. Ruuth, Master
of Oakland Lodge No. 188. The Grand Chaplain delivered the invoca.
tion.

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
Most Worshipful Ellsworth Meyer, Past Grand Master. acted as
Master of Ceremonies and the officers, elected and appointed, were in~
stalled by the retiring Grand Master in accordance with the Ritual.
The new Grand Master's lapel pin, presented by the members of
Summit Lodge No. 112, was transferred from the retiring to the newly
installed Grand Master; the previous Charles Albert Adams lapel pin
having been consigned to the archives of Grand Lodge. The other chair
officers then exchanged the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins.
The Robert B. Watts lapel pin was presented to the newly installed
Grand Chaplain by his predecessor, Reverend Max L. Christensen.
The retiring Grand Master was presented with a past Grand Master
pin by Most Worshipful Laurence E. Dayton, the apron of his new
designation by Most Worshipful Theodore Meriam. and a Past Grand
Master Certificate by Most Worshipful Ellsworth Meyer.
A gift was tendered Most Worshipful Eugene S. Hopp for his wife
by Very Worshipful Paul A. Pflueger on behalf of the members of
Grand Lodge. The junior Past Grand Master expressed his apprecia·
tion for the thoughtful gift to Mrs. Hopp and for the presentations to
him designating his new status as a Past Grand Master.
Most Worshipful Eugene S. Hopp thereafter presented to the newly
installed Grand Master a traveling case and expressed the hope that he
would flnd it useful during the coming year.
Following the installation ceremony, Grand Master Robert A. Crig·
ler introduced a number of the members of his Lodge who were present
as an indication of their fraternal regard. The newly installed Grand
Master then expressed his feeling of humility at having been accorded
this high M asonic honor and his appreciation to his many friends for
their support.
At 3:05 p.m .. all business being completed. Grand Lodge closed In
due form.

Basia of Accountings

The financial statements are 1tated on the cash basis of
accounting, Transactions generally are recorded at the time of the
receipt or payment of cash. current operating expense bills unpaid
were of a nominal amount.
The Grand LOdge previously purchased comprehensive liability insurance for participating Lodges, and was reimbursed by them.
In 1966 the Grand Lodge authorized per capita to include an amount
for in1urance premiums. The per capita was collected and the
in•urance expense was recorded during the current year. The
amount of prepaid insurance will be expensed in subsequent year•
as coverage expires .
In preparing the budget for 1968 th• Grand Lodge revised
certain expense classifications. The expenses of the prior year
have been recla.H ified in the attached financial statements to
make them canparable with the current year cla11ification.

JOBN ANO LENA LUCKENBACH FUND

The permanent endowment fund is restricted by Ordinances of Grand
Lodge so that no portion of the principal shall be expended for any
purpose, and the income therefrom shall be used only for the main•
tenance and general operation of the Masonic Hornes.

The principal, restricted by the terms of the Will, is to be kept
intact and the income used only for the benefit of the care of orphans
or the aged in Masonic Hemes of Southern California.

ANNUITY FUND

This fund, in the origina l amount of $30,000, is subject to a contract
with the donor providing for the payment of certain life annuities out
of the principal and income thereof. Under the terms of the contract.
only principal of the fund expended in payment of the annuities is to
be later restored out of income to the fund when the annuities no
longer absorb the entire income. After restoration of the principal
to the original sum of $30,000, the income from the fund is to be used
for the benefit of the residents of the Covina Home.

Land, buildings, and equipment are recorded at the cost
when originally purchased and no depreciation of buildings and
equipment has been provided for in the accounts. Replacements of
original itema of equipment are charged to operating expenses.
Prior to the current year, insurance premiums have been
expensed when paid. During the current year, certain policies were
paid for a three-year term. The unexpired portion of the premiums
has been recorded as an asset in the attached financial statements,
and will be charged to expense in subsequent years as coverage
expires.
Note 2.

Investments:

Investment in securities purchased are staced at cost;
securities received by gift or bequest are stated at approximate
market value at the date received, or at a nominal value of $1
if a market value at that date cannot be determined.

LIABILITIES:

Due to General Fund, Exhibit A

Basis of Accounting:

The financial statements are stated on a modified cash
basis of accounting. Transactions generally are recorded at the
time of the receipt or ?ayment of cash. Current operating expense
bills unpaid were of nominal amount.

recorded at the nominal value of $1 for accountability because
potential value is undetermined. Payment by Masonic Homes of loan•
previously obtained by the assignors on these assets are added to
the nominal value.

Reserves for Special Purposes:
